organizations/creative-studios/kamitsuba.heading: ## Operating Structure and Business Model
organizations/creative-studios/kamitsuba.body:
KAMITSUBAKI STUDIO positions itself as a “**creative label born on YouTube**,” and its operating structure differs structurally from that of a conventional talent agency:

| Dimension | How KAMITSUBAKI STUDIO does it |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Main platform** | By making YouTube its primary place of release, it **holds the power of media reach itself** and does not depend on established media channels |
| **Organisational form** | It **integrates in-house** the “label function of making music” and the “agency function of managing artists,” so that collaboration between artists can accelerate creative output |
| **Revenue structure** | Artists are the core, and revenue is **drawn from the fan community**; this is fundamentally different from the influencer-style model of “earning advertising fees from clients” |
| **Sales channel** | It adopts a **D2C (direct-to-consumer)** model, maximising profit margins without going through established distribution |
| **Reinvestment** | The profits generated by D2C are directed into music production, video and MV production, promotion, and returns to the artists |
| **In-house technology** | To integrate AR／VR／MR and other technologies and realise XR live performances in multiple forms, it **expands its technical staff and completes production internally** |

> **Difference from early VTubers**: KAMITSUBAKI STUDIO clearly distinguishes itself from “early virtual YouTubers, who were strongly role-play oriented and centred on performing a fictional character”—the defining trait of its artists is **an activity style centred on music with a strong documentary quality**.

> **Founding vision**: PIEDPIPER established and led KAMITSUBAKI STUDIO because he had discovered the talents of [Kanzaki Iori](/database/creators/kanzaki-iori) and [KAF](/database/artists/solo/kaf); the overall vision was to **build a YouTube-based creative label in Japan comparable to 88rising**, and through encounters with many creators and artists, that vision eventually took shape.

organizations/creative-studios/kamitsuba.heading: ## Organisational Restructuring and the Evolution of the Label System
organizations/creative-studios/kamitsuba.body:
| Date | Organisational event |
| :--- | :--- |
| 2019-10-18 | KAMITSUBAKI STUDIO is established on the first anniversary of KAF’s debut |
| 2023-07 | The **integration of SINSEKAI STUDIO** is announced, and the company is reorganised into a new four-label system |
| 2024-05-08 | **“ALLT STUDIO” and “PHASE STUDIO” are newly established**, and the transfer of some artists is announced alongside them |
| 2024-08-01 | Parent company THINKR completes a Series A round of roughly 5 billion yen, achieving fully independent operation (see [THINKR](/database/studios/thinkr)) |
| 2026-09-05 | THINKR announces a studio reorganisation (THINKR NEW STUDIO ARCHITECTURE): KAMITSUBAKI STUDIO **transitions into a label focused on the virtual domain**, and the labels within the studio are unified into [PHENOMENON RECORD](/database/studios/phenomenon-record); the real-world artists and creators of the former system are moved to newly established sibling studios such as [KYOKAI STUDIO](/database/studios/kyokai-studio) |

> **Repeated reorganisation of “labels within a label”**: From the four-label reorganisation of 2023 and the establishment of new studios in 2024 to the pivot to virtual focus in 2026, the organisational history of KAMITSUBAKI STUDIO shows a rhythm of **structural adjustment every one to two years**. This rhythm is matched to its long-cycle “music × narrative” IP strategy—the organisational form changes with the stage of each project rather than remaining fixed.

organizations/creative-studios/kamitsuba.heading: ## Affiliated Brands and Facilities
organizations/creative-studios/kamitsuba.body:
Beyond its core label, the KAMITSUBAKI system also includes several brands and facilities that carry different functions:

| Brand / Facility | Function |
| :--- | :--- |
| **KAMITSUBAKI RECORD** | KAMITSUBAKI STUDIO’s **predecessor music label** |
| **FINDME STORE** | The **mail-order store** for official merchandise |
| **TPNN** | A **fashion brand** |
| **KAMITSUBAKI CREATION** | A management guild for visual creators, MV directors and worldbuilding writers (see [KAMITSUBAKI CREATION](/database/studios/thinkr-creative-guild)) |
| **[PNDR](/database/studios/pndr)** | A self-developed digital music distribution platform and independent label established in 2024 |

> **Structural observation**: From “predecessor label → creative label → merchandise store → fashion brand → creators’ guild → distribution platform,” the affiliated brand matrix of KAMITSUBAKI STUDIO covers **four levels: production of works, sale of goods, fashion expression and industry infrastructure**. This “self-contained” brand structure and its D2C revenue model support each other—the label is both a content provider and its own distribution channel.
